cues.en: Our home is burning.
cues.zh: 我们的家园正在燃烧。

cues.en: Rapid climate change is destabilizing
cues.zh: 快速的气候变化正在动摇

cues.en: our world. It seems our emissions will not fall quickly enough to avoid runaway warming, and we may soon hit tipping points that will lead to the collapse of ecosystems
cues.zh: 我们的世界。我们的排放似乎无法足够快地下降，以避免失控的变暖，而且我们可能很快触及临界点，导致生态系统崩溃

cues.en: and our civilization.
cues.zh: 以及我们的文明。

cues.en: While scientists,
cues.zh: 尽管科学家、

cues.en: activists, much of the younger generation urge action, it appears most politicians are not committed to doing anything meaningful, while the fossil fuel industry still works actively against change.
cues.zh: 活动人士和许多年轻一代都在呼吁行动，但大多数政客似乎并不致力于做任何有意义的事，而化石燃料行业仍在积极阻挠变革。

cues.en: It seems humanity can't overcome its greed and obsession with short term profit and personal gain to save itself.
cues.zh: 人类似乎无法克服贪婪，以及对短期利润和个人利益的执迷，从而拯救自己。

cues.en: And so for many, the future looks grim and hopeless.
cues.zh: 因此对许多人来说，未来显得黯淡而绝望。

cues.en: Young people feel particularly anxious and depressed.
cues.zh: 年轻人尤其感到焦虑和抑郁。

cues.en: Instead of looking ahead to a lifetime of opportunity, they wonder if they will even have a future or if they should bring kids into this world.
cues.zh: 他们不再期待一生充满机会，而是在想自己是否还有未来，或者是否该把孩子带到这个世界上。

cues.en: It's an age of doom and hopelessness,
cues.zh: 这是一个充满厄运和绝望的时代，

cues.en: and giving up seems the only sensible thing to do.
cues.zh: 放弃似乎是唯一明智的选择。

cues.en: But that's not true.
cues.zh: 但事实并非如此。

cues.en: You are not doomed.
cues.zh: 你并非注定灭亡。

cues.en: Humanity is not doomed.
cues.zh: 人类并非注定灭亡。

cues.en: Despite the seriousness of the situation,
cues.zh: 尽管形势严峻，

cues.en: for years, positive trends have accumulated,
cues.zh: 多年来，积极的趋势一直在积累，

cues.en: and there is finally some good news and a clear path towards our collective climate goals. Welcome to our TED talk. Please watch this video to the end. Check out our detailed sources afterwards to learn more.
cues.zh: 而且终于有一些好消息，以及一条通往我们共同气候目标的清晰道路。欢迎来到我们的 TED 演讲。请把这个视频看到最后。之后查看我们详细的资料来源，了解更多。

cues.en: Okay. Let's start with the scariest things.
cues.zh: 好，让我们从最可怕的事情开始。

cues.en: Canceling the apocalypse.
cues.zh: 阻止末日。

cues.en: Some of the most widely shared stories about climate change are that it is an existential
cues.zh: 一些流传最广的关于气候变化的说法是，它是一种关乎存亡的

cues.en: threat, the end of human civilization,
cues.zh: 威胁，是人类文明的终结，

cues.en: and maybe even our own extinction event,
cues.zh: 甚至可能是我们自身的灭绝事件，

cues.en: and that it's basically unavoidable now. But what does science actually say?
cues.zh: 而且现在基本上无法避免。但科学实际上怎么说？

cues.en: As of 2022,
the global average temperature has risen 1.2 degrees Celsius compared to pre industrial times.
cues.zh: 全球平均气温较前工业化时代上升了 1.2 摄氏度。

cues.en: Limiting warming to 1.5 degrees was the most ambitious goal of the Paris Agreement, but we are not likely to meet it.
cues.zh: 将变暖限制在 1.5 度曾是《巴黎协定》最雄心勃勃的目标，但我们不太可能实现它。

cues.en: Already Already with the warming we have today, hot places will get hotter, wet places wetter, and the risk and strength of extreme weather events increase significantly.
cues.zh: 就在我们已经经历的变暖下，炎热地区会更热，潮湿地区会更潮湿，极端天气事件的风险和强度也会显著增加。

cues.en: Warming beyond two degrees makes all of these extremes more extreme.
cues.zh: 升温超过两度会让所有这些极端情况更加极端。

cues.en: Extreme weather events more common with more ecosystems under major pressure.
cues.zh: 极端天气事件会更常见，更多生态系统将承受巨大压力。

cues.en: Some will not survive.
cues.zh: 有些生态系统将无法存活。

cues.en: At three degrees, significant parts of Earth, especially in developing countries, might become unable to feed their populations.
cues.zh: 升温三度时，地球上大片地区，尤其是发展中国家，可能无法养活其人口。

cues.en: Heat waves will become a major global issue. Large scale natural systems will break down. The scale and frequency of hurricanes, fires, and droughts will further increase and cause trillions in damage.
cues.zh: 热浪将成为全球重大问题。大规模自然系统将会崩溃。飓风、火灾和干旱的规模和频率将进一步增加，并造成数万亿美元的损失。

cues.en: Poor regions and subsistence farmers will be hit the hardest.
cues.zh: 贫困地区和自给自足的农民将受打击最重。

cues.en: Hundreds of millions of people will need to leave their homes.
cues.zh: 数亿人将不得不离开家园。

cues.en: In the four to eight degree range, the apocalypse begins. The hothouse earth where things change so quickly that it may become unable to support our large human population
cues.zh: 在四到八摄氏度的升温区间内，末日就开始了。那是一个温室地球，变化如此之快，以至于可能无法支撑我们庞大的人口

cues.en: and billions may perish, leaving the rest on a hostile alien planet.
cues.zh: 数十亿人可能死亡，剩下的人则留在一个充满敌意的异星般星球上。

cues.en: A decade ago, for lack of action and perspective,
cues.zh: 十年前，由于缺乏行动和远见，

cues.en: many scientists assumed a four plus degree world was our future, and a lot of public communication focused on exactly this future path.
cues.zh: 许多科学家认为，升温4度以上的世界会是我们的未来，而大量公共传播也恰恰聚焦于这条未来路径。

cues.en: Luckily, it's much less likely that this version of the apocalypse will come to pass. If
cues.zh: 幸运的是，这种版本的末日成真的可能性已小得多。如果

cues.en: current climate policies stagnate,
cues.zh: 当前气候政策停滞不前，

cues.en: we're likely to end up with warming of around three degrees Celsius by 2100,
cues.zh: 到2100年，我们最终可能会升温约3摄氏度，

cues.en: which is scary and tragic and far from acceptable.
cues.zh: 这很可怕、很悲剧，也远不可接受。

cues.en: But this is actually good news.
cues.zh: 但这其实是好消息。

cues.en: How?
cues.zh: 怎么说？

cues.en: In the last decade, we've seen enough progress that most scientists now think that we have likely avoided apocalyptic climate change.
cues.zh: 过去十年，我们看到了足够多的进展，以至于大多数科学家现在认为，我们很可能已经避免了末日式气候变化。

cues.en: Although substantial risk still remains, we can pretty confidently say that humanity isn't going anywhere.
cues.zh: 尽管重大风险仍然存在，我们可以相当自信地说，人类不会消失。

cues.en: Civilization might have to change, but it will endure.
cues.zh: 文明或许必须改变，但它会延续下去。

cues.en: Which begs the question,
cues.zh: 这就引出了一个问题：

cues.en: what has changed over the last ten years, and is this really good news? The
cues.zh: 过去十年里发生了什么变化，这真的是好消息吗？那个

cues.en: invisible shift.
cues.zh: 看不见的转变。

cues.en: You probably know this story.
cues.zh: 你可能知道这个故事。

cues.en: The last decade has been an immense failure for climate policies around the world.
cues.zh: 过去十年，全球气候政策遭遇了巨大失败。

cues.en: Instead of passing comprehensive binding bills that would meaningfully reduce emissions, we mostly did nothing.
cues.zh: 我们没有通过能切实减排的全面且有约束力的法案，而基本上什么都没做。

cues.en: A lost decade with one negative record after another.
cues.zh: 这是失去的十年，负面纪录一个接一个。

cues.en: And this story is true, and it's one reason why so many people are giving up. But it is not the whole picture.
cues.zh: 这个故事是真的，也是这么多人放弃的原因之一。但它不是全貌。

cues.en: Despite the lack of climate policies and ongoing lobbying and misinformation campaigns from the fossil fuel industries, there was a lot of progress.
cues.zh: 尽管气候政策缺位，化石燃料行业又持续游说并散布不实信息，但仍然取得了大量进展。

cues.en: Let's go back twenty years to see why today is so different.
cues.zh: 让我们回到二十年前，看看今天为何如此不同。

cues.en: Between 2000 and 2010,
greenhouse gas emissions had grown by 24%,
cues.zh: 温室气体排放增长了24%，

cues.en: three times as much as the increase in the previous decade.
cues.zh: 是前一个十年增幅的三倍。

cues.en: Subsidies for fossil fuels aimed at promoting economic growth caused a colossal increase in their consumption.
cues.zh: 旨在促进经济增长的化石燃料补贴，导致其消费量巨幅增加。

cues.en: For developing countries like China and India, coal was the cheapest fuel for growth, while rich countries showed little interest in changing their ways.
cues.zh: 对中国和印度等发展中国家来说，煤炭是最廉价的增长燃料，而富裕国家则无意改变自身做法。

cues.en: In 2010, many people expected these trends to continue. Instead of decreasing fossil fuel use, its consumption would rise.
cues.zh: 2010年，许多人预计这些趋势会延续。化石燃料的使用非但不会减少，其消费量反而会上升。

cues.en: The next decade turned out to be very different though.
cues.zh: 然而，接下来的十年却截然不同。

cues.en: First of all, coal burning in developing countries like India has slowed down or leveled off like in China,
cues.zh: 首先，印度等发展中国家的煤炭燃烧已经放缓或趋于平稳，中国也是如此，

cues.en: and it's plummeted in rich countries like The UK and US.
cues.zh: 而在英国、美国等富裕国家，煤炭燃烧量则大幅下降。

cues.en: Since 2015,
cues.zh: 自2015年以来，

cues.en: three quarters of planned coal plants have been canceled, and 44 countries have committed to stop building them.
cues.zh: 四分之三的拟建燃煤电厂已被取消，44个国家已承诺停止建设燃煤电厂。

cues.en: Ten years ago, that would have seemed like wishful thinking, but today, we can say with confidence, coal is dying.
cues.zh: 十年前，这看起来像一厢情愿，但今天我们可以自信地说，煤炭正在走向消亡。

cues.en: It's just not competitive anymore because technologies we thought would remain expensive matured rapidly instead.
cues.zh: 它已经不再有竞争力，因为我们原以为会一直昂贵的技术，反而迅速成熟了。

cues.en: Renewable electricity has shown explosive progress.
cues.zh: 可再生电力取得了爆炸性进展。

cues.en: In a mere decade, wind energy got three times cheaper.
cues.zh: 短短十年间，风能便宜了三倍。

cues.en: Solar electricity is now 10 times cheaper.
cues.zh: 太阳能发电现在便宜了十倍。

cues.en: Cheaper than coal or any other fossil fuel burning power plant despite the massive subsidies and global infrastructure propping up fossil fuels.
cues.zh: 比煤炭或任何其他燃烧化石燃料的发电厂都便宜，尽管化石燃料仍获得巨额补贴和全球基础设施的支撑。

cues.en: 25 times more solar and nearly five times more wind electricity is produced today compared with ten years ago, which is, of course, not nearly enough.
cues.zh: 如今太阳能发电量是十年前的 25 倍，风电发电量也接近 5 倍，当然，这还远远不够。

cues.en: One of the biggest obstacles is the variability of their power output.
cues.zh: 最大的障碍之一，是其发电量的波动性。

cues.en: Renewables need a lot of energy storage to be a reliable power source, like expensive batteries.
cues.zh: 可再生能源需要大量储能才能成为可靠电源，比如昂贵的电池。

cues.en: Amazingly,
cues.zh: 令人惊讶的是，

cues.en: battery prices have decreased by 97%
cues.zh: 电池价格已经下降了 97%

cues.en: in the past thirty years, 60% in the last decade alone, which will serve all kinds of green technology like electric cars.
cues.zh: 在过去三十年里，仅过去十年就下降了 60%，这将支持电动汽车等各种绿色技术。

cues.en: You might say, well, that's great, but didn't Kurzgesagt's last climate video say that while wind and solar are nice, we need nothing less than a fundamental transition of our global industrial system?
cues.zh: 你可能会说，这很好，但 Kurzgesagt 上一个气候视频不是说过，风能和太阳能固然不错，但我们至少需要全球工业体系的根本性转型吗？

cues.en: Yes. But luckily, the shift goes beyond just the energy sector.
cues.zh: 是的。但幸运的是，这种转变不止发生在能源领域。

cues.en: Throughout the economy, people are working on improving current technology to lower emissions.
cues.zh: 在整个经济领域，人们都在努力改进现有技术以降低排放。

cues.en: We're rapidly replacing old incandescent light bulbs with LEDs that are 10 times more efficient.
cues.zh: 我们正在迅速用效率高 10 倍的 LED 取代老旧的白炽灯泡。

cues.en: about seven out of 10 new cars in Norway were electric or hybrid.
cues.zh: 挪威每 10 辆新车中约有 7 辆是电动车或混动车。

cues.en: it was already eight out of 10.
cues.zh: 这一比例已经达到每 10 辆中有 8 辆。

cues.en: And the list goes on from electric heating and better insulation to ships traveling at half speed to save fuel.
cues.zh: 这样的例子还有很多，从电供暖和更好的隔热，到为节省燃料而以半速航行的船舶。

cues.en: Wherever you look, you find scientists, engineers, and entrepreneurs
cues.zh: 无论看向哪里，你都会发现科学家、工程师和企业家

cues.en: trying to solve some aspect of climate change.
cues.zh: 正试图解决气候变化的某个方面。

cues.en: Enormous amounts of human ingenuity are being brought to bear on this problem with more and more people deciding to prioritize preventing rapid climate change.
cues.zh: 人类正把大量智慧投入到这个问题中，越来越多的人决定优先阻止气候急剧变化。

cues.en: Solutions for low carbon production of cement, electronics,
cues.zh: 水泥、电子产品低碳生产的解决方案，

cues.en: and steel, and innovations like artificial meat and carbon capture are in the works.
cues.zh: 以及钢铁，还有人造肉和碳捕集等创新，都在推进中。

cues.en: The more of these technologies we deploy, the cheaper new and better technology gets.
cues.zh: 我们部署的这些技术越多，更新、更好的技术就越便宜。

cues.en: The cheaper they get, the more people use them, and so on. We can see the impact already.
cues.zh: 它们越便宜，用的人就越多，如此循环。我们已经能看到影响了。

cues.en: The domestic c o two output of rich countries is falling without a major recession.
cues.zh: 富裕国家的国内二氧化碳排放正在下降，而且没有出现严重衰退。

cues.en: Since the year 2000,
cues.zh: 自 2000 年以来，

cues.en: the EU as a whole shows a 21%
cues.zh: 整个欧盟显示出 21% 的

cues.en: decrease, Italy 28%,
cues.zh: 下降，意大利 28%，

cues.en: The UK 35%,
Denmark 43%.
But the best news may be that emissions are no longer necessarily coupled with economic growth.
cues.zh: 但最好的消息或许是，排放不再必然与经济增长挂钩。

cues.en: In the past, this was an inconvenient
cues.zh: 过去，这很不方便。

cues.en: truth. To get richer, you had to emit more, which led to fierce arguments between developing and developed countries about the fairness of reducing emissions while their populations were still poor. But in the last decade, we've seen that it is possible to increase prosperity without increasing emissions.
cues.zh: 说实话，过去要想变得更富裕，就得排放更多。这导致发展中国家和发达国家之间争论激烈：当发展中国家的民众还很贫困时，要求他们减排是否公平？但在过去十年里，我们看到，提升经济繁荣的同时，也可以不增加排放。

cues.en: Emissions in The Czech Republic dropped 13%
cues.zh: 捷克共和国的排放量下降了 13%

cues.en: while their GDP grew by 27%.
cues.zh: 而他们的 GDP 增长了 27%。

cues.en: France reduced their c o two emissions by 14%
cues.zh: 法国的二氧化碳排放量减少了 14%

cues.en: while increasing GDP by 15%.
cues.zh: 同时将GDP提高15%。

cues.en: Romania saw an 8% decrease and 35%
cues.zh: 罗马尼亚下降了 8%，还有 35%

cues.en: growth.
cues.zh: 增长。

cues.en: And even the largest economy on earth, The USA,
cues.zh: 即便是地球上最大的经济体——美国，

cues.en: decreased emissions by 4% while growing their GDP by 26%.
cues.zh: 在实现排放量下降 4% 的同时，GDP 还增长了 26%。

cues.en: Some of you may call this a numbers trick,
cues.zh: 你们中有些人可能觉得这只是数字上的把戏，

cues.en: that rich countries are just exporting emissions to poorer nations by moving the dirty parts of their economies like manufacturing.
cues.zh: 富国只是通过把制造业等污染性产业转移出去，将排放出口到较贫穷的国家。

cues.en: But even when we account for all of our imported goods, the numbers still look positive.
cues.zh: 但即便把我们所有的进口商品都算上，数据看起来依然很乐观。

cues.en: It's no longer a matter of having to choose between prosperity and the climate as it seemed to be a decade ago.
cues.zh: 如今已不再像十年前那样，似乎必须在经济发展与气候之间做出取舍。

cues.en: Developing countries will profit from that because as rich countries pay for the expensive development of green technologies,
cues.zh: 发展中国家将从中受益，因为富裕国家为绿色技术的高昂研发费用买单，

cues.en: they can adopt them more cheaply. They can skip most of the high emission phase that today's rich countries went through.
cues.zh: 他们可以更低成本地采用它们。他们可以跳过当今富裕国家经历过的大部分高排放阶段。

cues.en: We are at the point where not decarbonizing
cues.zh: 我们已经到了不脱碳就……

cues.en: is a bad business decision.
cues.zh: 是一个糟糕的商业决策。

cues.en: And we haven't even really talked about solutions like carbon capture.
cues.zh: 我们甚至还没真正谈到碳捕集这类解决方案。

cues.en: In 2000, it didn't really exist.
cues.zh: 在2000年，它其实还不存在。

cues.en: that technology does exist and costs around $600
cues.zh: 那项技术确实存在，价格大约 600 美元

cues.en: to remove one ton of c o two from the atmosphere.
cues.zh: 从大气中去除一吨二氧化碳。

cues.en: As investment pours in and the technology matures and begins to scale, it's likely that these costs will plummet over the next few decades.
cues.zh: 随着投资涌入、技术日趋成熟并开始规模化，未来几十年这些成本很可能会大幅下降。

cues.en: So everything's
cues.zh: 所以一切都……

cues.en: fine then. Well, let's not get carried away. All of these processes are great, but not nearly fast enough. We're still doing way too little, and technology will not magically solve everything. We need to use fewer resources and use them longer, design consumer goods that are repairable and durable,
cues.zh: 那好吧。不过，别高兴得太早。这些流程都很好，但速度还远远不够。我们做的仍然太少，技术也不会神奇地解决一切问题。我们需要使用更少的资源，并更长久地使用它们，设计可维修、耐用的消费品，

cues.en: and decrease our energy requirements.
cues.zh: 并降低我们的能耗。

cues.en: We need much better infrastructure,
cues.zh: 我们需要好得多的基础设施，

cues.en: agriculture,
cues.zh: 农业，

cues.en: and cities.
cues.zh: 以及各个城市。

cues.en: It will still be hard work, especially to get the right policies passed and enacted.
cues.zh: 这仍将是艰巨的工作，尤其是要让正确的政策获得通过并付诸实施。

cues.en: But for the first time ever, there are a few trend lines pointing solidly in the right direction.
cues.zh: 但这是有史以来第一次，有几项趋势明确朝着正确的方向发展。

cues.en: And now imagine, if all of this was achieved without proper financial and political support, and despite fossil fuel lobbying, just think what humanity can do when climate change finally gets the political attention and funding it needs.
cues.zh: 现在想想，如果这一切都是在缺乏充足的资金和政治支持、还受到化石燃料行业游说阻挠的情况下实现的，那等气候变化终于得到应有的政治关注和资金支持，人类还能做到什么？

cues.en: So is it okay to feel hopeful again? The situation is still dire and serious, so what's the point of focusing on this side of the story?
cues.zh: 那么，再次怀抱希望是可以的吗？局势依然严峻而危急，那关注事情的这一面又有什么意义呢？

cues.en: The trap of hopelessness.
cues.zh: 绝望的陷阱。

cues.en: Climate change can feel overwhelming and make your future seem bleak.
cues.zh: 气候变化可能让人感到不堪重负，让未来显得黯淡。

cues.en: The sadness and hopelessness that many people feel is real and very destructive because it causes apathy.
cues.zh: 许多人感受到的悲伤和绝望是真实且极具破坏性的，因为它会导致冷漠。

cues.en: Apathy that is only serving the fossil fuel industry that is still delaying change however it can. In a sense, they have weaponized hopelessness.
cues.zh: 这种冷漠只会让化石燃料行业受益，而该行业仍在尽其所能拖延变革。某种意义上，他们把绝望武器化了。

cues.en: We are now in phase four in the public debate about rapid climate change action.
cues.zh: 在关于快速气候行动的公众讨论中，我们现在进入了第四阶段。

cues.en: Phase one was climate change is not real. Phase two was climate change is real, but not caused by humans.
cues.zh: 第一阶段是“气候变化不是真的”。第二阶段是“气候变化是真的，但不是人类造成的”。

cues.en: Phase three was climate change may be caused by humans, but it's not that bad. The phase four is climate change is no longer avoidable.
cues.zh: 第三阶段是“气候变化可能是人类造成的，但没那么糟”。第四阶段是“气候变化已无法避免”。

cues.en: We are doomed, and it doesn't matter what we do.
cues.zh: 我们注定完了，做什么都没用。

cues.en: If we want the world to change, we first need to believe that change is possible, and we have an abundance of evidence that it is.
cues.zh: 如果我们想让世界改变，首先需要相信改变是可能的，而我们有大量证据表明它确实可能。

cues.en: Changes to our industrial system are gaining momentum. Technology gets better and cheaper. Climate change has become a key issue in most free elections.
cues.zh: 我们工业体系的变革正在积聚势头。技术变得更好、更便宜。气候变化已成为大多数自由选举中的关键议题。

cues.en: As more and more younger people move into influential positions, they prioritize climate change and work on new solutions.
cues.zh: 随着越来越多年轻人进入有影响力的岗位，他们会优先考虑气候变化并致力于新解决方案。

cues.en: most governments not only acknowledge it, but set their own net zero goals in democratic and autocratic countries.
cues.zh: 大多数政府不仅承认它，还在民主国家和专制国家设定了自己的净零目标。

cues.en: The results of years of fighting a steep uphill battle are now clearly visible.
cues.zh: 多年艰苦卓绝的斗争成果如今已清晰可见。

cues.en: The pressure needs to keep increasing to make sure that the promises made today are actually kept.
cues.zh: 压力需要持续加大，以确保今天做出的承诺真正兑现。

cues.en: Climate doomerism is the equivalent of giving up, even though you can still prevent not just the worst case, but also mitigate most of the bad things, make changes in time to adapt better, and prevent the poorest from suffering.
cues.zh: 气候末日主义等同于放弃，尽管你仍然不仅能防止最坏情况，还能减轻大多数坏影响，及时做出改变以更好地适应，并防止最贫困者遭受苦难。

cues.en: That is why hopelessness and apathy
cues.zh: 这就是为什么绝望和冷漠

cues.en: are so dangerous.
cues.zh: 如此危险。

cues.en: If the last, in many ways, wasted decade has shown anything,
cues.zh: 如果说过去十年——在很多方面被浪费的十年——证明了什么，

cues.en: then it's that progress is being made, and that dire scenarios are just predictions,
cues.zh: 那就是进步正在发生，而可怕的情景只是预测，

cues.en: not our sealed fate. As of 2022,
cues.zh: 不是我们注定的命运。截至2022年，

cues.en: based on current global policies, we will end up in a three degrees world.
cues.zh: 根据当前全球政策，我们最终会走向一个升温三度的世界。

cues.en: Now it's our job to yet again prove the predictions wrong despite how serious and urgent things are. To turn that three degrees into a two degrees and then see where we can go from there. For that, we need hope.
cues.zh: 现在我们的任务是，尽管事情如此严重紧迫，仍要再次证明这些预测是错的。要把三度变成两度，然后看看从那里还能走到哪一步。为此，我们需要希望。

cues.en: And we hope we gave you that today, at least a little. That you feel that things are serious, but also that you have a future, that you could have kids without doing them or the world,
cues.zh: 我们希望今天至少给了你一点希望。让你感到事情很严重，但你也有未来，你可以生孩子，而不会害了他们或这个世界，

cues.en: that taking action today is worth it, and that despite powerful industries doing everything to delay it, society is changing.
cues.zh: 今天采取行动是值得的，而且尽管强大的行业竭尽全力拖延，社会仍在改变。

cues.en: If you need a more concrete road map of what you can do personally, we're working on a follow-up video to talk about that in greater detail.
cues.zh: 如果你需要更具体的个人行动路线图，我们正在制作后续视频，会更详细地讨论这一点。

cues.en: Dumerism,
cues.zh: Dumerism，

cues.en: inactivity,
cues.zh: 无所作为，

cues.en: and weaponized
cues.zh: 以及被武器化的

cues.en: are
cues.zh: 是

cues.en: the only trump cards left for the powers that don't want change.
cues.zh: 不愿改变的势力仅剩的王牌。

cues.en: Don't let them win.
cues.zh: 别让他们得逞。
